- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 2–5%.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > +5% above recent mean), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3–4% above prior peak.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.3) and price is trending down, model frequently underestimates; add 1–3% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment swings; smooth 3–5 day moving average of forecast before final output.
- When sentiment alternates between high/low, model exhibits lagged response; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days if sentiment shifts sharply.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overpredicts early in the window; reduce first 5–7 days’ forecast by 1–2% to align with observed mean reversion.
- If sentiment is high but price is falling, model may misread sentiment; treat as “contrarian” signal and reduce forecast by 1–3% to avoid overconfidence.
